claims.finding: The statute expressly names USIA, Broadcasting Board of Governors, International Broadcasting Bureau, and Secretary of State. State Department is the selected organization endpoint for functions vested in the Secretary.

Sections 1311 and 1312(b) exclude BBG, IBB and their functions from abolition/transfer to State; section 1322 continues the existing BBG. These are retained broadcasting functions, not a newly created board or a transfer from State.
Section 1312(a) transfers USIA/director/component functions to the Secretary of State, subject to section 1312(b) broadcasting exceptions.

results.functionsTaken: the surviving economic regulation: rail rate and service regulation and the residual carrier jurisdiction the Act recodifies into subtitle IV, chartered as the Board (ICCTA title II)

the functions the Act vests in the Secretary: carrying out the recodified motor-carrier part (49 U.S.C. 13301(a): 'Except as otherwise specified, the Secretary shall carry out this part') and the carrier-related consumer-protection enforcement the conforming amendments redirect (ICCTA secs. 314-316)

claims.finding: Section 2 makes the Act effective January 1, 1996 except as otherwise provided. Sections 101 and 201 abolish ICC and establish STB; cited provisions do not state a different date for those changes.
The Act names ICC and STB and assigns separate functions/personnel to the Secretary of Transportation. Transportation Department is the selected organization endpoint for those Secretary functions.
Section 102 recodifies Board rail jurisdiction including rates/services and residual carrier matters; section 201 establishes the Board; section 203(a) moves resources for Board functions.

Recodified 49 USC 13301(a) directs the Secretary to carry out the motor-carrier part except as otherwise specified; sections 314-316 redirect the specified consumer-protection enforcement; section 203(b) separately transfers resources for Secretary functions.
